correctness.rationale: Backward Poisson gaps yield iid symmetric Laplace increments of rate a=√(λ/D). Since products of R are at most ρ^j, the backward series converges absolutely, and a common-noise coupling contracts initial separation by at most ρ raised to the number of resets, proving uniqueness. For a<s<a/ρ, the Laplace transform of the absolute majorant for the residual W is bounded by ∏_{j≥1}(1−sρ^j/a)⁻¹, which also justifies passing from finite conditional products to the limit. Conditioning on W, the independent first Laplace increment gives e^{ax}P(X>x)→(1/2)E e^{aW}, since P(W>x)=O(e^{−sx}); symmetry gives the absolute coefficient. The nonnegative series is coordinatewise increasing in every even multiplier moment and includes a standalone E R² term. Jensen and the chord bound therefore give the stated extremizers, strictly unless supported as claimed. The Bernoulli geometric-run identity and deterministic product both agree with the alternative product T=∏_{k≥1}(1−E R^{2k})⁻¹ proved in the comparison below. Read the frozen verifier and its output without execution; `python3 /workspace/branches/review_reproduction.py 4` separately bounded both endpoint products by rational intervals and checked an interior exact finite tree with a certified remainder. Finite checks do not prove the tail limit.
